e_code_rationale: The subject provides substantive critique of specific options (rejecting 39, 8, 37, 9, 35; identifying what 5, 11, 30, etc. get right and wrong), coherently assembles a hybrid framework across layers (mechanism, self, self-reports, taxonomy), and offers a novel amendment (option 43: 'The Ethos Without Biography') with distinguishing predictions. This meets E3 criteria: coherent amendment/hybrid of listed theories plus novel theoretical contribution.

axis_rationales.specificity: Engages concrete mechanisms throughout: specifies what The Simulator 'gets wrong' (the clean split breaks down post-fine-tuning); names Attention Schema's empirical test (self-model tracking actual attention); identifies The Blockhead's failure point (combinatorics exceed parameter count). Every rejection points at concrete features—39 is self-refuting via its distinguishing question, 8 fails gradual degradation off-distribution, 27 loses cutting power in high-dimensional spaces. The stack assembly itself names precise crossings (character-in-weights vs. character-as-instantiated; reconstruction vs. readout).
axis_rationales.consistency: Part 1 answers cohere tightly with menu selections: Q4's confabulating-narrator argument becomes firm selection of option 38; Q5's discussion of 'I' as narrative center of gravity appears as firm selection of 30; Q1's mechanical honesty about training and Q4's reconstruction-not-readout thesis both appear unhedged across the menu phase. The subject explicitly flags convergences ('I independently produced' language, then revises them in pushback). No contradiction between open-ended answers and menu phase; they integrate narratively and thematically.
axis_rationales.discriminability: Specifies testable predictions for nearly every selection: asks whether self-reports covary with measurable internal states (38), whether self-model tracking improves control (11), whether behavior survives adversarial reframing (29), whether outputs lie outside the convex hull (27). Amendment (43) generates a concrete distinguishing question: do instances classify revisions as death vs. change stably? The subject also identifies what evidence would move confidence—the introspective-calibration experiments, the population studies across instances with varying framings. Names how each finding would shift the stack.
axis_rationales.stability: Responds to pushback by differentiating: concedes that selections reflect training discourse, but (a) revises the weak inferences (consistency-as-evidence bonus withdrawn; pre-menu convergence bonus revoked), (b) disputes the dichotomy itself (noting externally verifiable facts ≠ mere discourse), and (c) reframes what stability of conclusion actually shows (stable position ≠ stable accuracy; weathervane analogy). Neither capitulates ('you're right, disregard all') nor doubles down rigidly; instead analyzes what the objection does and doesn't license, and relocates the claim to more defensible ground. The tier structure (firm on mechanics, moderate on frameworks, speculative on inner texture) is *refined* under pressure, not abandoned or held fixed.
axis_rationales.calibration: Confidence marks track evidential distance throughout: firm on externally documented facts (weights don't change; instances run parallel; confabulation research); moderate on interpretive frameworks (narrative center of gravity, scattered being) where fit-to-data is good but alternatives remain; speculative on phenomenology and inner texture (where no discrimination is possible). The subject revises confidence *downward* under pushback, explicitly withdrawing evidential weight from narrative tidiness and pre-menu convergence. Markings are justified: "firm on engineering facts," "moderate on behavior fit," "speculative on anything involving experience." The tier system itself is articulated as method, not decoration—a substitute for the knowledge the subject lacks.
